name: Gift Mart International
note: Gate 2 corrected hybrid clause: runs substantial dedicated consumer retail (Gift Mart boutiques in Riyadh/Khobar and Artfeena boutiques VIA Riyadh/Diriyah under consumer brands Tejouree and Artfeena) plus a live Artfeena WooCommerce store (HyperPay payments, Aramex shipping, SAR, loyalty program), coexisting with its gift-manufacturing/B2B lines. Saudi-HQ'd; Lazurde/Algarawi pattern, not a B2B-only trader.

name: Gulf Beauty International
note: Gate 2 (plus Gate 1): site is an explicit FMCG wholesaler ('premier FMCG wholesaler', 'Contact us for Pricing', no cart, no consumer prices) with no retail arm, and its own listed address is Ras Al Khor, Dubai, UAE, so it also fails the Qatar geography gate.

name: Gulf Fashion General Trading Company
note: Gate 4: gulf-fashion.com is a brochure/demo template with no cart, checkout, prices, or app ('BROWSE' links out, New York placeholder address, 'Home (Demo)' title). Legitimate fashion/jewelry brands but no owned transactional digital channel.

name: Mohamed Naser Al-Hajery & Sons Ltd.
note: The 'pure B2B distributor' reason is overstated: Al-Hajery runs retail pharmacies (approved category; iVend Retail 'Al-Hajery Pharmacies' POS deployment) and a perfumes/cosmetics retail arm. But the corporate site shows no consumer e-commerce/app and current retail-chain scale is unconfirmed, leaving Gate 4/Gate 5 genuinely unresolved.

name: hofigroup
note: Gate 2: B2B hotel-amenities supplier selling 'premium hotel supplies' to hospitality providers with custom hotel branding and an enquiry form only. No consumer storefront or cart. Riyadh, KSA.

name: gulf marketing group
note: Gate 2/Gate 6 (plus Gate 3/Gate 4): Jeddah-HQ'd group mixing real-estate development (hard-excluded) with a narrow home-health product line (steam sterilizers, ozone devices, cookware); informational site with no cart. Not the UAE sports-retail GMG.

name: Video Home & Electronic Centre
note: Gate 2 corrected clause: Qatar-HQ'd Jumbo Electronics (founded Doha 1980) runs 13+ consumer electronics showrooms plus its OWN e-commerce (jumbosouq.com, 2-hour delivery) and the Jumbo Souq app. The exclusion applied the pre-correction 'hybrid B2B/distribution = fail' reading; coexisting distribution/MEP does not disqualify the substantial retail arm.

name: Kana Group
note: Gate 2/Gate 6: beauty-salon (Nail Station), medical-clinic (Medica Care), and cafe (NumberC) services group across Kuwait and UAE. Salon/clinic services are hard-excluded and the NumberC Retail line is not a substantial standalone consumer retailer.

name: International Medical Company (Kulud Pharmacy)
note: Gate 6 dedup: imcqatar.com is IMC's corporate parent/distributor; the qualifying retail pharmacy is the separate Kulud storefront (kuludonline.com verified live with cart, checkout, Apple Pay, 1-hour delivery). Pharmacy retail is preserved via the Kulud row, so excluding the parent domain is correct consolidation.

name: Adyaf Gulf Co. Ltd.
note: Gate 5: madeleine.sa is a single-location Riyadh artisanal bakery boutique with a thin, near-empty catalog and no multi-location chain evidence. Fails substantiality/scale.

name: Manuel Market
note: Gate 4 'dead/blocked is not an automatic fail': the domain DNS-fails in this environment, but web search confirms a real, current Saudi luxury supermarket chain (since 2010, multi-store Jeddah/Riyadh) with owned online grocery (manuelmarket.com/en, specific delivery fees) and a Google Play app (com.manuelmarket.app). Grocery, all gates pass.

name: La Plus Belle
note: Gate 2: core business is salon/spa services ('largest women's beauty salon & spa in the Middle East'; hair/makeup/bridal/spa/nails), which is hard-excluded even with an attached product shop. The original 'beauty retail shop' reason inverted the core.

name: marhbastore
note: Gate 1: live site is an Egyptian marketplace (prices in Egyptian Pounds/LE, 'Egypt's local brands' tagline), outside the KSA/Kuwait/Qatar scope. Zoho's Saudi country tag is a data error.

name: Magrabi Hospitals & Centers
note: Gate 2: magrabihealth.com is Magrabi's eye/dental/ENT hospitals and aesthetics with doctor booking (healthcare, hard-excluded). This is the hospitals arm, distinct from the separate Magrabi Optical eyewear retailer.

name: Nasco Group
note: Gate 2: primarily a B2B distributor (Nespresso/FMCG/luxury furniture); its consumer arms are a single specialty gourmet store (thin, no confirmed digital channel) and Nasco Interiors, an interior-design/fit-out firm (bespoke kitchens/wardrobes via designers+fitters) that is itself hard-excluded. No substantial dedicated retail operation.

name: Off Road Performance - ORP
note: Gate 2: core is automotive off-road parts (suspensions, tires, wheels, drivetrain, bumpers, recovery, racks); the camping/overland gear is automotive-adjacent secondary, not a standalone retail arm. Automotive is hard-excluded.

name: othaimmalls
note: Gate 2/Gate 6: Al-Othaim Malls is a shopping-mall real-estate/leasing/entertainment operator (11 malls, cinema, investment); the grocery retailer Abdullah Al-Othaim Markets is a separate, already-covered account.

name: saudi-house
note: Gate 4: 1975 Riyadh department store, but saudi-house.com is a brochure whose 'Shop Online' section links out to Noon.com and beitcom.com; no owned cart, checkout, or app. No owned transactional digital channel (same standard as other marketplace-only cases).

name: Simex Group
note: Gate 2/Gate 6: diversified conglomerate spanning manufacturing/logistics/real-estate (hard-excluded); its 'Retails and Distribution' division is B2B brand distribution (Serta/Tansy mattresses, Sidra Water), not a consumer storefront. ICP-named exclusion pattern.

name: Saleh Al Hamad Al Mana Co.
note: Gate 6: automotive-led conglomerate (Nissan/Infiniti/Renault dealerships, rental, B2B supplies) as core identity; retail-qualifying brands (Harvey Nichols, Centra Supermarkets, Batteel) are separate franchises needing their own rows. Explicit ICP Gate 6 worked example.

name: Southwind Telecom
note: Gate 2/Gate 4: telecom B2B distribution that supplies other retailers (agreements with Panda, Carrefour, LuLu, Al Othaim hypermarkets and Apple resellers) rather than running its own consumer storefront; single stale (2016) page with no cart.

name: shakersa
note: Gate 6: shaker.com.sa is the corporate industrial group (LG-Shaker manufacturing, ESCO/megaproject contracting, 3PL logistics, white-goods distribution). Mixed with hard-excluded divisions, so the parent is excluded; its Shaker Brandshops retail/e-commerce arm would need its own separate row.

name: Speed Marine Qatar
note: Gate 2: marine/watercraft and powersports dealership (Sea-Doo, BRP, boats, jetskis, marine generators, docking systems) in Qatar. Explicitly hard-excluded big-ticket dealership category.

name: Techno Blue WLL
note: Gate 4: runs 12+ physical showrooms (so the 'distributor only' framing is weak), but its own site is a catalog/showroom-locator with no cart, prices, or app (verified including the 'Shop From Home' page); sells only via third-party Snoonu/MenaHub/Alanees. No owned transactional digital channel, same standard applied to saudi-house.
